elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information about significant people (e.g. family members, friends and teachers) such as their relationship to the student, physical appearance and characteristics, for example, interviewing or introducing people; describing a person from a photograph

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: agreeing or politely disagreeing with each other’s opinions or negotiating changes when working together and discussing topics related to the school environment and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing information about social activities, festivals, special community celebrations or school events, for example, creating posters; writing captions for images; writing a short speech using modelled sentence structures

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing interests, routines and social activities when participating in teacher-moderated online exchanges with sister schools in target language-speaking contexts, such as secure video blogs

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: sustaining interactions with others by asking questions, using active listening skills (e.g. eye contact, body language, repeating back what they hear), and providing feedback such as advice or reminders to peers about their learning experiences, for example, participating in role-plays; interviewing someone; sharing opinions about topics during small-group discussions

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a simulated interview with someone they consider a role model, such as a sports figure, a musician, artist, teacher, family member or friend

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: accompanying spoken texts with appropriate gestures, facial expressions, body language and formulaic expressions that are culturally relevant, for example, presenting information about their local area as a video blog for a simulated online platform; presenting information about the school environment as a virtual school tour

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging print or digital greeting cards for significant occasions such as birthdays or to invite, congratulate or thank someone, or responding to an email from a new penfriend in a country or region where the target language is spoken, using suffixes, diminutives or terms of endearment (where relevant) to indicate affection and familiarity with names of pets or family members

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C01-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and answering questions about familiar topics (e.g. school, family, hobbies), using interrogatives or conjugating verbs depending on personal pronouns (if relevant), for example, creating a role-play script for an interview with another student

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6C02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion and planning with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information to organise a meeting with friends, discussing where and when the event will take place

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: allocating roles, planning and creating displays or resources such as timelines, schedules or posters for class, school and community events

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: making print or digital invitations and arrangements for a shared event or experience such as a class party, receiving visitors to the school or a film afternoon

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the currency used in a country where the target language is spoken and identifying the current exchange rate, noticing how much familiar items cost in each currency

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using imperative forms of verbs to give instructions or tell others about procedures, such as giving instructions during a game or class activity

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking and responding to questions, and asking for repetitions or clarification using repair strategies, such as ‘Pardon?’, ‘I’m sorry, I didn’t understand’, ‘Could you please repeat that?’, ‘Could you say that again more slowly?’

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning a real or imagined trip, using expressions related to place, time and numbers, agreeing on itinerary and a packing list

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning a campaign, for example, to introduce healthy culturally varied food at the school’s multicultural event(s), to raise awareness about pollution or to promote harmony and positive relationships, and creating posters, pamphlets and flyers or making presentations to the class or parents and school community members

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and participating in role-plays related to everyday situations such as purchasing grocery items, requesting information about train or bus timetables, asking directions to a place in town, bargaining at a market, buying souvenirs or ordering food

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C02-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning for a guest interview by a speaker of the language by developing a list of questions with peers, or preparing performance texts together to present to younger students at a community event or school assembly

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6C03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering and comparing information from different sources on topics such as family life, cultural trends, children’s social activities, community or schooling in Australian contexts and in countries or regions where the language is spoken, and sharing their learnings with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and presenting information from a range of print and digital resources about features of their local environment (e.g. water, bush care, ecosystem, wildlife) and sharing these in simulated blog or social media posts, brochures or posters

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: consulting teacher-curated online catalogues and websites, comparing prices and values of different objects (e.g. food, clothing, travel), discussing intended purchases and budgeting for imagined shopping expeditions

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing an image of students eating lunch at a school in a country or region where the language is spoken and completing a ‘word, phrase, sentence’ thinking routine using information from the image, then discussing their notes with a partner

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing traditional folktales, contemporary stories and/or cartoons, and then responding by retelling or re-enacting the story in their own words, or by sequencing images or creating captions to summarise or retell the story in the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing their reactions to imaginative texts that evoke responses such as sadness, fear or excitement, and relating them to their own experiences by using stem statements, for example ‘That reminds me of a time when …’, ‘I remember when I …’, ‘I knew someone that …’, ‘We learned about this in …’

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting interviews with family members or friends, or watching documentaries or video clips to collect stories about migration to Australia, then identifying words and expressions that reflect important values and feelings associated with the stories and sharing their findings with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing different types of texts (e.g. debates, documentaries, short animated films, news stories) and then using graphic organisers (e.g. sequence-of-events chains, mind maps) to process the content, main ideas and/or characters that were shown

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C03-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: accessing information from websites, books or magazines about important celebrations and festivities in a country or community where the target language is spoken, extracting the main points, and providing a summary of the key messages of the texts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6C04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in the target language in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information from a range of print and digital resources about social and cultural activities in their local community, then making a list of terms, expressions or behaviours, such as welcoming the guests by standing up, and waiting for those older than themselves to start eating

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying signage from their local area and interpreting and comparing it to signage in a country or region where the language is spoken, for example, comparing traffic and road signs or signs in public places, and then creating versions of Victorian school signs and notices in the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting factual information related to cultural activities, for example, daily routines, celebrations, sporting events and concerts

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and reading a range of text types (e.g. phone conversations, emails, invitations, articles), then discussing their characteristics and features such as style, language and structure

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying loan words and phrases used in the target language in domains such as food or music or in a selection of teacher-curated texts from social media, and discussing how the target language reflects contemporary and global influences

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning to use bilingual print and digital dictionaries, identifying issues such as multiple meanings for words and that meaning is not always literal, and/or recognising how different word types (e.g. nouns, verbs, adjectives) are identified in the dictionary

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering English words and expressions (e.g. music, guitar, fire, sport, earthquakes) used in other curriculum areas, and applying strategies to convey the meaning in the target language, for example, saying a sentence using the new word and then acting out the word for a partner to guess

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how language is adapted to reflect levels of politeness and formality and to reflect relationships, age and intention, for example, watching video clips and identifying formal and informal language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing movements, facial expressions, gestures and actions to interpret meaning in texts, identifying key messages and amusing moments, and practising using these strategies when conversing with a partner, participating in a role-play or presenting to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C04-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting examples of proverbs in the language (e.g. proverbs used at home by background language learners, where relevant) and discussing how to explain their meaning to non-target language-speaking friends, then reflecting on times when their use of the target language, English and/or other languages has been misinterpreted and discussing possible reasons for this

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6C05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a menu for a meal, which may include footnotes in English to explain characteristics and ingredients of the dishes

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a class print or digital poster locating and describing, in the target language, a specific Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching and discussing the advantages of being able to communicate in more than one language, and creating an interactive presentation for younger children, friends or members of their extended families to showcase their bilingual/multilingual experience and how this has been beneficial

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use all forms of the present tense of regular verbs and of high-frequency irregular verbs, for example, when writing an email to a friend explaining what they do and don’t like to eat, or presenting a floor plan and description of their house to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating digital profiles of characters they enjoy in different stories, plays or poems, providing descriptions of physical appearance and character traits and examples of the ways they speak and behave

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing texts to entertain others, incorporating elements such as dance, mime, singing and narration, and referencing values and traditions associated with communities that speak the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing texts and compiling lists of informal language and expressions for everyday interactions with friends and family

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: writing a postcard or simulated travel blog in the present tense to share with others, about an imaginary holiday to a different state in Australia or to another country, and including information about mode of transport, accommodation, length of stay, weather, leisure activities and cultural sites, or writing the script for a fashion show, using appropriate text type conventions and conjunctions, cohesive devices or comparatives to evaluate and express opinion

elaborations.name: VC2LR6C05-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: giving, following and planning directions, for example, listening to instructions while ‘driving’ a toy car along the streets on a map, demonstrating understanding of a range of prepositions to indicate direction or location, and then creating a script of directions for a simulated interactive GPS experience

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6U01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency and rhythm in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising differences in the pronunciation of long and short vowels (if relevant), understanding that the length of a vowel can change meaning, and understanding that tone marks or other accent marks can change the sound of a letter, for example, looking at words or sentences and identifying long and/or short vowels and accent marks, and discussing how these can change sound and meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reciting poems that exemplify a certain vowel pronunciation or phoneme and practising the word endings

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how pitch, stress and rhythm help to convey meaning even if individual words are unfamiliar, by listening to different sentences and discussing their observations

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing intonation and fluency of set phrases in a shadow-speaking activity, for example, listening and then speaking along to a recording, gradually reducing the sound of the recording until only their own voices can be heard

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to use emphasis to enhance meaning, for example, using high-pitch tone and primary stress at the ends of words, and practising this by saying or reading simple phrases or sentences to a partner, changing their tone and emphasis and discussing what they observed

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying the principles of vowel harmony, sound assimilation of consonants and grammatical knowledge to the spelling and writing of unfamiliar words

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the pronunciation of loan words, including vowels and consonant clusters, and identifying common morphemes (where relevant), for example, repeating or reading a range of loan words in the target language, practising the correct pronunciation as a class, with a partner or by recording themselves, and listening to their pronunciation when played back

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the effect of non-verbal language and tone in reinforcing meaning in spoken language, for example, listening to video clips without watching them and writing down what they think the meaning is, then watching the video clip (including sound) and identifying how their interpretation has changed and why

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how variations in language use reflect different feelings, moods or attitudes, for example, watching a video and discussing the variations in language and how they contributed to feelings, moods or attitudes

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U01-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: adapting modelled examples of tongue twisters to experiment with a range of letter combinations and sounds

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6U02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: beginning to use all forms of the present tense of regular verbs and of high-frequency irregular verbs, for example, writing an email to a friend explaining what they do and don’t like to eat; presenting a floor plan and description of their house to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the conjugation of auxiliary verbs (if relevant), for example, reading sentences with different pronouns and completing a ‘think, pair, share’ activity, identifying the rule for conjugating each verb

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using nominal conjugations through adjective- and noun-making prefixes or suffixes (if relevant), for example, reading and identifying the relevant features in a text, annotating the text, then using the examples to write sentences of their own

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of nouns, including more unusual plural forms, as well as more complex adjectives and possessive forms, and applying the rule of major vowel harmony when adding nominative case endings to different nouns (if relevant)

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reinforcing grammatical rules for gender agreement (if relevant) or agreement between verbs and subject, by playing games such as matching nouns and subject pronouns or pairing the subject with a conjugated verb

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using a range of adverbs (e.g. places, days of the week, seasons) when participating in word-order games, writing simple sentences or responding to questions using modelled grammatical structures

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sentence-builder charts to support the development of longer sentences that include a range of clauses to sequence ideas or add further information, using a range of adverbs to elaborate or accentuate meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using prefixes or suffixes (e.g. unfriendly) and varying forms of negation (e.g. no, not, none), for example, collecting a card with a sentence in the positive form and rewriting it in the negative, such as ‘I have (no) brothers and sisters.’

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying, explaining and applying the rules for creating comparative adjectives, for example, rewriting sentences using positive adjectives to include the comparative; viewing images and describing what they see using comparative adjectives; responding to questions about their likes and dislikes, such as ‘Maths is more interesting than sports’, ‘My sister is older than my brother’

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that particles (if relevant) express relationships between elements within a sentence, and applying them in accordance with grammar rules, according to context, for example, completing a particle fill-the-gap activity

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E11 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple, compound and some complex sentences, and recognising different types of formal and informal, respectful or honorific forms of the language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E12 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising definite and indefinite articles (if relevant), and noticing that they can be singular or plural, for example, listening to sentences read by the teacher and placing hands on heads for definite articles and hands on hips for indefinite articles

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E13 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding (if relevant) the use of prefixes and suffixes and duplication to express plurality in nouns

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E14 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the use of prepositions in sentences to indicate time, place, location or direction by describing objects or events, for example, describing what they do at different times of the day or describing the location of an object in the room

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U02-E15 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding patterns for forming and using ordinal numbers (if relevant), for example, when deciding the turn order in a card game or reordering objects according to the teacher’s instructions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6U03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare structures and features of the target language with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising words in the target language that may be similar to English and/or other languages, and identifying false friends (where relevant) and how they can lead to difficulty when learning the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing language used in texts, for example, descriptive language in recounts or narratives; humorous language in comics and some poems; persuasive language in advertisements; instructional language in recipes and manuals; expository language in news reports

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing characteristic features of texts (e.g. the use of abbreviations and emojis in texting, rhetorical questions in advertisements, numerical terms in recipes and receipts, emotive and rhyming words in song lyrics, headings on websites, imagery in creative texts), and identifying how they help to convey meaning and engage the audience

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how poems or song lyrics in the language create moods and tap into particular emotions by using techniques such as repetition, rhyme and direct forms of address, and compare with techniques used in poems and song lyrics in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: talking about grammatical structures and how they are used, using metalanguage, for example, identifying word classifications (e.g. noun, verb, adjective, personal pronoun) and grammatical structures (e.g. word order, tense) when reading and annotating texts such as emails

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage to discuss the features of familiar text types, for example, a shopping list includes items and some numbers; a role-play at a market involves interaction and negotiation; an email or text message to a friend involves interaction and an exchange of information

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing feedback during peer assessment, using metalanguage, for example, editing each other’s written or spoken texts and work samples, making recommendations related to the language use and justifying their reasons

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning basic metaphors, similes and common idiomatic expressions and proverbs, and comparing these with figures of speech in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing verb conjugations in the target language and English and/or other known languages and identifying patterns in conjugation

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U03-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some loan words in the target language originate from Aboriginal languages from different areas around Australia, for example, ‘koala’ comes from the Dharug word gula, meaning ‘no water’, and ‘dingo’ comes from the Dharug word din-gu, then comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR6U04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this has an impact on verbal, non-verbal and written communication
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how language use reflects respect and social distance, such as making requests with different levels of formality or showing respect for authority figures

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying adjustments they make when moving between the language and English and/or other languages at school and at home (where relevant), such as using different forms of address, gestures or expressions to show respect or affection

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on how interacting in the language feels different from interacting in English and identifying elements that feel culturally specific

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing traditional methods that speakers of the language use to preserve language and culture, comparing these with examples of dances, songs, artworks, artefacts or traditions from a range of different cultures, and identifying how they strengthen connections to values and identity, for example, discussing the significance of a possum-skin coat for some Aboriginal Peoples and sharing similarities and differences between cultural artefacts in other languages and cultures represented in the classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that people interpret and respond to intercultural experiences in different ways depending on their own cultural perspectives, recognising the validity of different perspectives and questioning notions of ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ ideas or behaviours

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering how many regular interactions reflect cultural practices and values associated with family life, food and social relationships, for example, greetings; table manners at mealtimes

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the meaning of ‘culture’, how it involves visible elements such as ways of dressing, eating and dancing, and less-visible elements such as ways of thinking and valuing

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring teacher-curated examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and discussing how identity and gender are represented in the language

elaborations.name: VC2LR6U04-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the idea of generalisations associated with languages and identities, discussing how groups of people tend to think about themselves and others, and how stereotypes affect attitudes and communication and can be inaccurate

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Roman Alphabet Languages - Levels 7 and 8 (Curriculum F-10 Sequence)

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 7 and 8, learning of the target Roman alphabet language builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. They work increasingly independently and in groups, and continue to receive feedback and support from their peers and teachers. Students use the target language, in person or online, to interact and collaborate within and beyond the classroom. They listen, speak, read, write and view to exchange information, ideas and opinions about their worlds. Background language learners and second or additional language learners may also interact and collaborate within and beyond the classroom to facilitate learning.

Students access a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts from a variety of authentic sources, which may include audio and video clips, magazines, advertisements, images, stories and articles. Background language learners may source texts and other resources from their local community to share with peers. Students use their knowledge of some metalanguage in an increasing range of contexts to reflect on similarities and differences between the structures and features of the target language, English and/or other languages.

Students recognise that language choices reflect cultural values, beliefs and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 8, students initiate and maintain target language interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to a range of interests and experiences. They use the target language to collaborate and problem-solve, and adjust their language in response to others. They interpret information, ideas and opinions in texts. They demonstrate understanding of the similarities and differences between languages, in both familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, by adjusting and reorganising responses. They sequence information and ideas, and select and use vocabulary, sentence structures and expressions to create texts appropriate to context, purpose and audience.

Students apply the conventions of the spoken language and continue to enhance fluency. They demonstrate understanding that spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts use different conventions, structures and features to convey meaning. They comment on structures and features of text in the language, using some metalanguage. They reflect on how the language, culture and identity are interconnected and compare this with their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.elaboration_text: using the internet to research young people’s lifestyles across cultures and contexts, or using secure digital tools to engage with target language-speaking students around the world, collecting and comparing information to identify the influence of factors such as geography, climate, and social and community environments

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C03-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: gathering information about well-known people in fields such as sports, entertainment, pop culture, the arts or history who speak the target language, to create a profile to present to their peers

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C03-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to popular song lyrics or viewing current television programs and comparing representations, values and social commentary with those conveyed in traditional short stories and novels

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C03-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR8C04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the importance of body language in communication and that there are culturally specific meanings associated with body language, and then discussing what they have learned about body language when speaking the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: brainstorming useful strategies to use when listening to audio texts, such as listening for keywords or using a guided note-taking sheet to identify different types of language in authentic texts (e.g. podcasts, radio, television programs and advertisements) and then producing a written or verbal response, such as responding to short-answer questions, writing an informative post for a simulated blog or recording a video blog about text types for other target language learners

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying language associated with cultural categories such as family life, clothing or superstitions when analysing short texts in the target language, noticing when expressions require an explanation

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying reading strategies when reading texts, for example, identifying keywords in a sentence to interpret meaning or to look up in a dictionary to help establish meaning quickly

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing short excerpts of folktales, stories, songs or plays and collating examples of culturally relevant elements that cannot be translated easily into English, for example, the opening phrases of fairy tales or the closing of stories

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing variations in language use according to context and relationship, for example, identifying differences in exchanges in English and in the target language, such as formal language, colloquialisms, slang or idioms typically used by young people, such as ‘Apologies for any inconvenience caused’, ‘Not at all’, ‘No worries’

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading or listening to short texts and comparing their own understanding with their classmates, then discussing reasons for variations and discrepancies

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading, recognising and annotating features of language used in different texts that reflect the intended purpose and audience, such as statistics used in informative writing, rhetorical questions used in persuasive writing, opinions and feelings used in personal writing

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering why some topics of conversation may be approached differently in the target language and in English, and adjusting language appropriately, for example, watching a film excerpt and reflecting on the similarities and differences between the use of language, body language, facial expressions, volume, tone and/or eye contact

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C04-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting language samples that show how people vary their language use and word choice based on their relationships with others, different situations, social status and cultural backgrounds, and recording examples in their books, for example, language used by teachers to students; language used by students to students; politicians’ speeches to the electorate

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR8C05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, sequencing information and ideas, selecting vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures appropriate to text type and context

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information gathered from different media sources to raise awareness or invite action on a social or community issue such as language learning in Australia, a healthy lifestyle or environmental pollution, using a combination of print, sound, images and hyperlinks

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting on good news items such as successful fundraising activities or academic or sporting achievements, via posts on the school website or segments on local radio

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining modes of presentation such as displays, video clips or music to present an overview of community cultural themes, for example, family life; hospitality; relationships

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school, a guide to their favourite place, an explanation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Country and Place names, or a history of their town

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating subtitles, captions or commentaries for texts such as video clips, displays or slide-show presentations that introduce the school community to significant aspects of cultural and national celebrations

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating with peers to create imagined scenarios between contemporary versions of characters or events encountered in traditional literature or songs

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting an imaginative text that they enjoy, such as a poem or song, and adapting it to a different text type, writing style or genre such as a rap, an advertisement or a children’s story

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts to share with younger learners, such as big books or comics, incorporating humorous and expressive language

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using appropriate digital tools to create and present an informative oral or written history of a significant older person in their family or community who speaks the language

elaborations.name: VC2LR8C05-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with alliteration, repetition and wordplay by creating their own tongue twisters, poems, raps or songs on selected topics

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR8U01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply conventions of the spoken target language to enhance fluency, and to respond to and create texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to audio or multimodal texts and identifying where the speakers place stress in complex sentences, then replicating the intonation patterns in their own spoken texts

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the pronunciation of long and short vowels with and without the tone or accent marks (if relevant), and how the length of the vowel and/or accent can change the meaning of words

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to a tongue twister, proverb or song and understanding any sound assimilation in the spoken language that does not exist in the written form

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising pronunciation of vowels and consonant clusters in loan words, for example, taking turns with a partner to draw cards with a loan word written on them, then saying the word as their partner listens and provides feedback, before swapping roles and repeating the process

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying homophones in the language and learning how different homophones affect meaning in sentences, for example, reading sentence cards with homophones on them and discussing the differences in meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with rhythm and tempo in the recitation of poems, developing understanding of the function of stress and applying it to unfamiliar words and phrases in more complex sentences and texts

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and explaining the different levels of formality in both spoken and written language, and then creating a list of the type of language used in a person’s interactions with different people at various times and places during their day (e.g. when they are at home with family, at school or buying something at the shops), then creating a table of different word forms to show changes in the keywords, using vocabulary based on familiar topics

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying phonemic knowledge and grammatical knowledge to spelling and writing unfamiliar words, for example, using letter combinations and words involving 2 or more distinct vowel sounds, practising identifying the sounds when playing bingo, and then moving to saying the sounds, words and sentences containing the letter combinations

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U01-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising syllable emphasis on words that are spelled the same but pronounced differently in English and in the target language, for example, listening to the word, recording themselves saying the word with the appropriate emphasis, and then listening to it played back and reflecting on any further improvements they could make

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR8U02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending their knowledge of negative constructions by collecting question cards, and then moving around the room and asking other students a question that they must answer using a negative construction

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences between tenses, for example, reading sentences or short texts, highlighting all of the verbs, brainstorming which tense each verb is in (e.g. present, past or future) with a partner and checking understanding during a class discussion, or identifying verb prefixes or suffixes and explaining their function

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using adjective endings appropriate to number or gender (if relevant), for example, explaining the rules for adjective endings to a partner; completing fill-the-gap activities; including adjective endings appropriately when responding to texts, such as expressing an opinion about a video clip

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using active and passive verb forms in simple sentences, for example, organising sentence cards into active and passive columns; rephrasing passive sentences into the active voice; reading a simple text in the active voice and rewriting it in the passive voice

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating texts that include a range of formal and informal language suited to different audiences, for example, writing the script for a role-play between an older person and a young person, emphasising the differences in language choices for each character in the script

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying commonly used false friends (where relevant) and creating an infographic to explain the origins of the words

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a range of texts for a specified context, purpose and audience, using more complex conjunctions or cohesive devices to sequence ideas and actions, to improve cohesion, and to compare and contrast, for example, writing a blog post for the school community informing them about the importance of recycling

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using imperative verb forms to give instructions or directions to others, or using negative forms of the imperative to explain rules, and responding using a range of interrogative word forms, for example, writing instructions for how to make a cake, or advice about how to balance school and hobbies

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating longer sentences by adding further information, using a range of adverbs of time or place (e.g. this morning, on the weekend, in the city, at school), or creating compound or complex sentences that use clauses to sequence information and ideas, for example, writing sentences by building on sentence starters or using word-order mnemonics

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: conjugating verbs in different tenses to form new words and phrases, and applying understanding of word order for simple and compound sentences, for example, participating in group spelling races in which they aim to be the first group to correctly spell a word in a different tense using mini-whiteboards or letter cards

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E11 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using known vocabulary and relevant verb forms to express possibility, obligation and ability, for example, writing an email to a friend talking about what they want to do but are not able to because they are obliged to do something else

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E12 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different types of formal and informal honorific terms or respectful forms of the language

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E13 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a range of pronouns, such as possessive pronouns to indicate ownership or relative pronouns to differentiate, for example, playing a card game in which they turn over 2 cards, a pronoun card and an object card, then create a sentence using both

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U02-E14 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using singular or plural articles in the language (if relevant), for example, telling the time or talking about days of the week

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR8U03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on the structures and features of the target language, and compare them with English and/or other languages, using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining self-corrections and editing choices using metalanguage, for example, using a checklist to review their own draft and complete a self-assessment task, then redoing the task, incorporating their own feedback, and reflecting on how they improved

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing language for monitoring, describing and reflecting on using the language in intercultural experiences, for example, completing a running dictation with sentence starters (e.g. ‘I see …’, ‘I wonder …’, ‘In the future I will …’, ‘I am not yet confident with …’) in the target language, then participating in ‘I do, we do, you do’ sentence-writing activities, focusing on intercultural experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying grammar and vocabulary in the target language and using metalanguage to refer to different elements (e.g. noun, verb, adjective, adverb, present tense, past tense, pronoun), and comparing them with the vocabulary and grammar in English or other languages they know

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the diversity of accents, dialects and vocabulary in target language-speaking communities with similar examples of diversity in other countries

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the format and stylistic conventions of different texts in the target language and English and/or other languages, such as ways of addressing the audience in formal and informal speeches or letters and emails, and ways of signing off

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key features of familiar types of texts (e.g. print and digital public announcements, commercials, advertisements, itineraries) in the target language and comparing these to English to help understand unfamiliar content

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing examples of text types in the target language, English and/or other languages, such as horoscopes, menus, advertisements or weather forecasts, explaining the use of particular language features

elaborations.name: VC2LR8U03-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing how texts in the target language and English establish register, by identifying words and expressions that suggest degrees of formality, audience and context

field_grouped_levels_per_subject.name: Roman Alphabet Languages - Levels 9 and 10 (Curriculum F-10 Sequence)

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 9 and 10, learning of the target Roman alphabet language builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. They continue to receive guidance, feedback and support from their peers and teachers. Students use the target language to initiate and sustain interactions that communicate their own and others’ experiences of the world. They listen, speak, read, write and view to communicate with other speakers of the language in local and global settings through authentic community and secure, teacher-moderated online events. Background language learners and second or additional language learners may also support each other in their literacy development.

Students access and create written and spoken texts, increasingly of their own choice. They access an increasing range of authentic and purpose-developed resources, which may include textbooks, audio and video clips, feature articles, television programs, social media and other multimodal texts. Background language learners may source resources from their local and global communities to share with peers.

Students expand their knowledge and control of the structures and features of the spoken and written language. They acknowledge that there are diverse influences on communication and cultural identity, and that these influences can shape their own behaviours, values and beliefs.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 10, students contribute to and extend interactions in the target language in increasingly unfamiliar contexts related to a wide range of interests and issues. They interpret and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in texts. They contribute to discussions involving diverse views, negotiate outcomes and compare experiences. They demonstrate understanding of how features of language can be used to influence audience response. They create texts, selecting and manipulating language for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences. They apply and use complex sentences and structures to create and respond to spoken and written texts. They use a variety of tenses to sequence events and use language features to enhance meaning and cohesion.

Students incorporate features and conventions of the spoken language to enhance and extend fluency. They demonstrate understanding of the conventions of spoken and written texts, in both formal and informal contexts, and the connections between them. They apply knowledge of language, structures and features to make and predict meaning. They analyse target language texts using metalanguage. They reflect on their own cultural perspectives and identify and draw on their experience of learning the language to evaluate how this learning influences their ideas and ways of communicating.

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring concepts related to their own and each other’s social worlds, such as equity, the environment or gender roles, or global issues such as diversity, explaining their views in terms of values and expectations and using descriptive and expressive language, for example, viewing images and completing a ‘word, phrase, sentence’ thinking routine, then expressing their opinions about what they have learned from the image

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing aspirations in relation to social, educational and professional futures, including consideration of the role that languages will play in these projections, for example, researching future careers and whether it would be possible to work in this profession in a country where the target language is spoken, then discussing their findings as a class

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing their peers about their opinions on effective communication, focusing on issues such as their use of social media and their use of different languages in different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: acknowledging elements of others’ arguments or challenging ideas in a respectful manner, for example, revising language used for negotiating or debating and using this in role-plays, discussions or debates

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking peers questions that require the use of analytical or comparative language in response, for example, discussing a film, image, audio or written text and comparing information within or between texts or with their own experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: sustaining and extending exchanges by responding to questions that encourage reflection and require the use of language to reflect opinions (e.g. ‘I believe …’, ‘my opinion is …’, ‘I was surprised that …’) and evaluation (e.g. as a result of, due to, therefore, in contrast to)

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C01-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending exchanges by giving encouragement, criticism or praise to peers in debates or discussions

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR10C02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: contribute to discussions that involve diverse views to negotiate outcomes, address issues and compare experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating a particular course of action, for example, planning a day out with a homestay guest; creating an itinerary for a group of visitors; celebrating an important festival with the school community

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: organising real or simulated forums to raise awareness of environmental, social or ethical issues

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining information in order to debate issues of interest such as the environment, expectations of adolescents and the generation gap, or cultural practices such as marriage or rites of passage, using persuasive or evaluative language

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating a ‘language and culture’ day or celebration, discussing what was successful and what needs to be changed or improved

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in discussions about issues that affect their lives at school, home or in the community, and comparing their experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating arrangements, compromises or alternative ways of achieving common outcomes, for example, negotiating plans for the holidays with friends or role-playing a discussion with their parents about the possibility of getting a part-time job

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing issues related to their own and each other’s experiences such as diversity, identity, health and wellbeing or technology, and sharing their views, values and expectations

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using persuasive language to encourage a change of opinion, for example, writing a persuasive article or creating a targeted advertisement

elaborations.name: VC2LR10C02-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages F-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a news clip or part of an informative video and using what was introduced in the clip as a prompt for discussion, for example, summarising the main points and then providing and justifying their own opinions
