elaborations.elaboration_text: considering register when using elision of sounds, syllables or words in spoken texts, to ensure that language use is appropriate to the context and audience, for example, comparing conversation conventions when talking to a friend compared to when talking to a teacher

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using homophones in spoken and written texts and learning how these affect meaning in sentences and in familiar idioms, for example, reading a short text, identifying the homophones and discussing the different meanings

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: varying the use of tone for emphasis or to contribute to cohesion during extended spoken interactions, for example, reading a short dialogue with a partner or small group several times, each time changing the tone to emphasise different elements

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: building fluency and accuracy of pitch, stress, rhythm, pronunciation and intonation by listening to and reciting increasingly longer spoken texts or participating in choral reading activities

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reproducing rhythms in more complex sentences, using pauses and intonation to signal clause sequence and emphasis, for example, recording themselves reading short texts several times, altering the pauses, intonation and emphasis, then analysing what worked well

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: adjusting the tone, register and word choice of spoken or written language to reflect the formality of the context, for example, reading a dialogue, with a partner, between a young person and an older neighbour, then repeating the dialogue, making appropriate changes to the language and tone to reflect a conversation between 2 teenage friends instead

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding spontaneously to questions from their teacher or peers on both familiar and unfamiliar topics, using gap fillers where needed

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL01-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using sentence starters and connecters to increase the complexity of ideas and responses, for example, asking a question and listening to the response, then asking a follow-up question such as ‘I found … really interesting, could you tell me more about that?’

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR10UL02 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of context and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts that include some complex structures, ideas and conventions appropriate to formality and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different auxiliary and modal verbs for different purposes, such as to express different tenses or to express necessity or possibility when responding to or writing texts, or identifying and using prefixes or suffixes for modality

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and correctly applying conventions for punctuation and tone or accent marks (if relevant) in their own writing

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using particles (if relevant) and complex conjunctions to extend fluency when creating texts, for example, completing worksheets with 2 sentences and a conjunction and connecting the sentences using the supplied conjunction and the appropriate grammatical structures

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using superlative adjectives and noticing patterns when using them, for example, writing an evaluative or persuasive article giving opinions about an event or a film

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying rules for word order and sentence structure to demonstrate grammatical agreement (if relevant) in a range of simple and compound sentences, for example, completing sentence-unjumbling games in pairs or small teams

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying how adverbs (e.g. time, manner, place), adverbial phrases or determiners are used for describing people, places, objects and experiences, for example, reading a text about a student’s daily routine and identifying the adverbs and discussing word order; writing short texts about their own daily routine

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and applying rules for creating the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives, for example, comparing 3 sentences containing comparative adjectives and brainstorming the rule, then applying this knowledge by rewriting positive sentences into the comparative or describing a holiday to a partner

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and using more complex verb tenses, compound and complex sentence structures (e.g. main and subordinate clauses) and parts of speech to describe, recount, reflect, inform and express opinions, for example, writing an email to a friend describing their holiday, an article informing exchange students about the school or a blog post expressing an opinion about wearing school uniforms

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and using a variety of verbs (e.g. reflexive verbs) or verb forms (e.g. imperative, conditional), for example, participating in a sentence-unjumbling activity; rewriting sentences in a different form; responding to or writing a text such as a blog post about their daily routine

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using adjective endings appropriately for number or gender (if relevant), for example, reading a text and highlighting the adjective endings; discussing why adjective endings may be similar or different; participating in adjective-ending challenge games or writing sentences or texts using adjectives

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E11 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing understanding of how a range of noun, verb and adjective endings can be used to form new words and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E12 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of text type conventions and grammatical features such as articles, quantifiers and particles (if relevant) to produce a range of text types appropriate to context, purpose and audience

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E13 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying a range of pronouns when creating texts, for example, using pronoun substitutes; conjugating pronouns; using pronouns when referring to something already mentioned

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E14 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using cardinal numbers (if relevant) to express increasingly larger numbers and to measure, describe percentages and fractions, and estimate, noticing patterns in their use, for example, planning a budget to redecorate a room; calculating distance between places; representing data on graphs

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL02-E15 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the use of prepositional phrases to compare and contrast concepts and ideas, for example, evaluating the use of technology in the classroom

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR10UL03 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and evaluate texts, using metalanguage to discuss language structures and features

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage, in the language or in English, to identify grammatical differences between languages, such as word order, conjunctions, tenses, verb forms, pronouns

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and developing metalanguage for talking about forms and functions of language, for example, identifying and explaining different types of sentence structures relating to grammatical functions such as predicates, subjects and objects

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying ways that texts in the language and English achieve cohesion, for example, explaining the effects of paragraphing or cohesive devices used to sequence and link ideas and maintain the flow of expression

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the intended purpose and audience of texts by analysing language features and text structures, such as colourful and persuasive language in advertisements compared with economical, factual language in product labelling or signage, and applying their understanding to the composition of their own texts

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing the use of rhetorical devices and emotive language to engage the intended audience in texts such as slogans or speeches

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding when to use various tenses, and comparing them with equivalent tenses in English or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spoken and written texts such as apologies or invitations to identify how differences in grammar and text-type features determine the nature of formal and informal interactions, for example, reading or viewing texts and discussing the differences as a class

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how grammatical choices shade meaning and establish register to distinguish relationships, for example, annotating a supplied text, reflecting on and discussing the changes in meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that false friends (where relevant) can cause misunderstandings or confusion, for example, identifying examples of false friends in a range of texts and discussing why they lead to misunderstandings

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL03-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the prevalence of acronyms and their use for convenience, for example, reading teacher-curated social media posts and then identifying and discussing different acronyms in the texts

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LR10UL04 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
substrand_content_descriptions.text: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E01 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: keeping a journal of memorable experiences associated with learning and using the language in and out of school, noting personal reactions and reflections over time and insights gained into themselves as language users, such as how they choose to use the target language or English and/or additional languages in different contexts and situations

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E02 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying elements of their personal worlds that contribute to their sense of community and identity, including their use of different languages and involvement in different cultural practices

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E03 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and/or reading examples of an Acknowledgement of Country in the target language, then creating their own version that names the local Country for an audience of people who speak the target language

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E04 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing a selection of song lyrics, poems, idioms and expressions, identifying how they may convey cultural values and reflect social, political and historical influences and events

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E05 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the concept of identity and that some speakers of the language who identify as non-binary may choose to use gender-neutral language where available, highlighting the dynamic nature of languages

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E06 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the diversity of spoken language forms from region to region and between different target language-speaking communities around the world, considering how language variation can both reflect and shape social and cultural contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E07 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing and discussing the interconnected nature of the linguistic and cultural diversity of the target language-speaking world, and how this is also relevant to the linguistic and cultural diversity in Australia, including that of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E08 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the influence that language can have on inclusivity and identity, for example, the language used in art, graffiti, or a teacher-curated selection of texts from online media

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E09 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing intercultural experiences and challenges, and sharing personal reactions, comparing aspects of identity that may be important

elaborations.name: VC2LR10UL04-E10 - Roman Alphabet Languages 7-10
elaborations.elaboration_text: appreciating that language use can reflect and express cultural identity, that multiple languages exist in many regions of the world and Australia, including Indigenous languages, and that many people are multilingual and value this capability as an integral part of their identity
